name.text: Even and Odd Functions — reading symmetry from a graph (JSXGraph)

questiontext.text:
The graph of \(y=k(x)\) is shown below.

[[jsxgraph width="420px" height="360px"]] var scenario = {#scenario#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-5, 8, 5, -8], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); var f; if (scenario === 0) { f = board.jc.snippet('0.3*x^2+1', true, 'x', true); } /* even: symmetric about y-axis */ else if (scenario === 1) { f = board.jc.snippet('0.1*x^3-1.5*x', true, 'x', true); } /* odd: symmetric about the origin */ else { f = board.jc.snippet('0.2*x^2+0.6*x', true, 'x', true); } /* neither */ board.create('functiongraph', [f, -4.5, 4.5], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2}); [[/jsxgraph]]

Based on the symmetry of the graph, is \(k(x)\) even, odd, or neither?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text: An even function's graph is a mirror image of itself across the \(y\)-axis. An odd function's graph looks the same after a \(180^\circ\) rotation about the origin. If neither of these holds, the function is neither.

falsefeedback.text: Check carefully: does folding the graph along the y-axis map it onto itself (even)? Does rotating it 180 degrees about the origin map it onto itself (odd)? Or neither?
